transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We're from Redwood Inference, I'm Maya, AE; with me are Carlos, our SE, and Priya who helps with identity and enterprise setups. Quick intro?
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Jordan here, Head of IT at Atlas HealthTech. Joining are Avery our CISO and Samir our Identity engineer.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Awesome. High level for today's call, we want to review SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning flow and go over RBAC and least privilege patterns — make sure it lines up with your SOC2/ISO requirements.
[00:33] Avery Chen: Yep, mainly interested in SAML 2.0 with SP-initiated flow, SCIM for provisioning, groups mapping into RBAC, and audit logs. Data residency is also a hard requirement — PHI-ish workloads, so we need encryption at rest + KMS integration details.
[00:48] Carlos Jimenez: Great, we can walk through the typical setup. Quick note — some of the auto-transcript might call our product Redwood Private or Redwood Dedicated interchangeably; we use the same SSO surface across hosted/dedicated/private with some config differences.
[01:05] Samir Gupta: How do you handle SCIM group deprovisioning? We need immediate disable when removed from IdP.
[01:12] Priya Rao: SCIM delta syncs by default; we support immediate user disable on deprovision events. There's a short delay depending on provisioning intervals but for Atlassas's needs we can push near-real-time via webhook hooks or more frequent polling. (note: polling interval configurable).
[01:28] Jordan Lee: Are service accounts required for SCIM? What's the least privilege model for that account?
[01:33] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, you create a SCIM service account in Redwood with token scoped to provisioning only. Principle of least privilege: scope tokens to 'user:write,user:read,group:read' — do not give admin or model management scopes. We can show recommended IAM scopes in the guide.
[01:50] Avery Chen: And what about SAML attributes? We want role mapping based on groups, not custom attributes.
[01:56] Priya Rao: We recommend group-to-role mapping. Example: IdP group 'ai-engineers' maps to Redwood role 'model-deployers' with least-priv permissions. We'll share a sample mapping JSON and SCIM group attribute mapping.
[02:12] Samir Gupta: Audit logs — retention, export, and tamper-proofing? We have regulatory obligations to keep logs for 7 years in some cases.
[02:20] Maya Patel: For hosted customers we provide audit logs with configurable retention; default is 90 days but we have add-ons for longer retention. Logs include SSO events, provisioning, role changes, and API key events. We support pushing logs to your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch/Event Hubs or S3 archive.
[02:40] Avery Chen: Do you support signed, append-only logs or WORM storage for compliance?
[02:45] Carlos Jimenez: We don't yet ship a native WORM store, but we support S3 with Object Lock for compliance and can push to an append-only external system. We can also provide integrity checks and signed digests on request for enterprise contracts.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: KMS — we use AWS KMS with CMKs in our account. Can Redwood use our KMS for customer-managed keys?
[03:09] Priya Rao: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for private deployments and for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM solutions). For hosted we offer a BYOK flow for enterprise where key material is controlled by your account and we use a key-wrapping pattern. We'll attach a diagram in the docs.
[03:28] Samir Gupta: When an employee leaves, we want immediate revocation of all sessions and tokens. How does session termination work with SSO?
[03:36] Carlos Jimenez: We support immediate session revocation through the SCIM deprovision + token revocation API. There's also an option to enforce short-lived tokens so sessions expire quickly; we can tie session length to your SSO session TTL.
[03:48] Avery Chen: On RBAC, we need separation of duties. Example: deployers shouldn't be able to change billing or audit settings. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[03:58] Maya Patel: RBAC is role-based and resource-scoped. Out of the box we have roles like Owner, Admin, Model-Deploy, Billing-Viewer, Audit-Viewer. You can create custom roles and scope them to projects/environments. We'll provide a least-privilege matrix.
[04:15] Jordan Lee: Is role assignment only via SCIM group sync, or can admins set roles manually?
[04:20] Priya Rao: Both. You can assign via SCIM group mapping for automated provisioning, or an admin can set or override roles in the console. We recommend SCIM for scale and auditability.
[04:32] Samir Gupta: Is there an audit trail for manual overrides?
[04:35] Carlos Jimenez: Yes — every role change, manual or via SCIM, emits an audit event with who, when, and previous/new values. Those are shipped to audit logs in near-real time.
[04:47] Avery Chen: Encryption at rest and in transit — standard TLS for transit, AES-256 at rest? Any FIPS validated options?
[04:55] Priya Rao: TLS 1.2/1.3 and TLS mutual-auth where needed; AES-256-GCM at rest. For FIPS/HSM we support integrating with FIPS validated HSMs in our Private/Dedicated offerings. We'll include specific cipher suite details in the security whitepaper.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: Data residency: can we ensure data stays in EU region with customer-managed keys?
[05:17] Maya Patel: Yes, region pinning is available in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have region controls for where data is stored; with enterprise contracts we can do strict residency and KMS in customer account in the EU region.
[05:30] Samir Gupta: How about penetration testing and vulnerability disclosures?
[05:34] Carlos Jimenez: Redwood runs quarterly internal pentests and annual 3rd-party assessments. We share a redacted report under NDA and have a coordinated disclosure program. SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestations are available for customers under an NDA link.
[05:50] Avery Chen: Can you walk us through an example SCIM mapping during the call?
[05:54] Maya Patel: Sure — example: IdP group 'atlas-ml-ops' => SCIM group 'atlas-ml-ops' => Redwood role 'model-deployer' (permissions: model.deploy, model.view, logs.view). We'll send the JSON mapping and a sample IdP metadata XML.
[06:12] Samir Gupta: What about group nesting? We use nested groups in AD — do you flatten or support nested group expansion?
[06:18] Priya Rao: We flatten nested groups via the SCIM sync; we can also read memberOf attributes in SAML assertion if your IdP includes them. There's a caveat with group depth and performance but it's supported.
[06:32] Jordan Lee: If we automate provisioning, do you create accounts or just link SSO identities?
[06:37] Carlos Jimenez: We create linked Redwood accounts tied to federated identities. If a user doesn't exist, SCIM creates them (provision) and assigns groups/roles. No passwords are stored for federated users.
[06:49] Avery Chen: What about emergency access / break glass? We need a process that still enables emergency model rollbacks but is audited and requires multi-person approval.
[06:58] Maya Patel: We support break-glass roles which require approval workflows. For the highest privileges we can require two-party approval in the console and log those events as high-severity audit entries.
[07:12] Samir Gupta: Anything about rate limiting or throttles on SCIM so provisioning storms don't bork the system?
[07:18] Priya Rao: We have throttles and a backoff mechanism. For large orgs we suggest bulk provisioning via our bulk SCIM endpoint to avoid throttles; we'll share guidance.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: For the pilot, we want a scoped project that only has model inference, not access to training data or billing. Can you create scoped projects?
[07:36] Carlos Jimenez: Yes, projects are scoping primitives. You can scope models, keys, and roles to a project. Billing is separate and only visible to Billing-Viewer or Owner roles. We'll show a project-level demo in the follow-up.
[07:50] Avery Chen: Last question — incident response and RTO/RPO expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[07:56] Maya Patel: Hosted has SLA tiers with RTO targets for service and per-route latency SLOs. Dedicated has stricter RTOs and placement controls. We'll include an SLA matrix and incident runbook summary in the packet.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: Great.
[08:15] Maya Patel: Quick recap of next steps — Maya will send SSO/SAML config guide + SCIM mapping, Carlos will stand up demo tenant, Samir will share IdP metadata, Avery will confirm retention requirements. We'll schedule the hands-on demo next week.
[08:30] Avery Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:33] Maya Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite.
[08:36] (call ends)

Summary: Security-focused review covering SSO (SAML 2.0), SCIM provisioning and group mapping, RBAC patterns and least privilege, audit log retention and export, KMS/BYOK integration, data residency options, and incident/SLA differences between Hosted/Dedicated/Private offerings. Action items and next steps captured.
